Patient: Dana Whitfield   DOB: 03/14/1972   MRN: 00482231
Callback: (555) 201-4478

Subjective: 54 y/o F with low back pain radiating down the left leg to the lateral foot for 11 weeks. Started physical therapy on 08/10/2026, 2x weekly, and has completed 14 sessions. Taking naproxen 500 mg BID since 08/04/2026 with partial relief. Leg pain persists despite therapy and now limits walking to about one block.

Exam: Positive straight-leg raise on the left at 40 degrees. Decreased sensation over the left lateral foot (S1 dermatome). Left ankle reflex diminished compared with right. Strength 5/5.

Assessment: Left lumbar radiculopathy, likely S1, not improving after 8 weeks of physical therapy and NSAIDs.

Plan: Request MRI lumbar spine without contrast to evaluate for disc herniation before considering epidural steroid injection.

Assessment: Severe right knee osteoarthritis with functional limitation.

Plan: Patient wishes to proceed with right total knee arthroplasty.
